extracted.intended_audience: mathematics researchers, academic job applicants, and AMS prize nominators (AMS community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and professional standards for submitting academic job applications (use of the AMS standard cover sheet and recommended employer responses) and for preparing nominations for AMS prizes (eligibility windows, categories, and required supporting materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: JCEO hiring response standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The JCEO believes that every applicant is entitled to the courtesy of a prompt and accurate response that provides timely information about his/her status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the JCEO urges all institutions to do the following after receiving an application: (1) Acknowledge receipt of the application immediately; and (2) Provide information as to the current status of the application, as soon as possible. The JCEO recommends a triage-based response, informing the applicant that he/she (a) is not being considered further; (b) is not among the top candidates; or (c) is a strong match for the position.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS Standard Cover Sheet — usage and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Add this Cover Sheet to all of your Academic Job Applications. The form is provided as an aid to departments in processing job applications; include it on top of your application materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to use: Using the facing page or a photocopy (or a TeX version from e-math), fill in answers that apply to all applications, make photocopies. As you mail each application, fill the remaining questions neatly on one cover sheet and include it on top of the application. Do not send this form to the AMS. Purpose: to aid department staff in tracking and responding to each application. Contact: dmm@math.ams.org or Professional Programs and Services Dept., AMS, 800-321-4267 ext. 4105.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS Standard Cover Sheet — required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover sheet specifies the applicant information departments expect to receive with applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields and instructions (from form): Last Name, First Name, Middle Names, Social Security Number (optional), Address through June 1996, Home Phone, e-mail Address, Current Institutional Affiliation, Work Phone, Highest Degree and Source, Ph.D. Advisor, If Ph.D. not held, expected date, Indicate mathematical subject area(s) using the 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification (printed on back), Primary Interest, Secondary Interests (optional), Brief synopsis of current research interests (avoid special mathematical symbols, do not write outside boxed area), Most recent post-Ph.D. position (university/company, position title, dates), Indicate position applied for and posting code, Would you like to be considered for temporary positions? (options), List up to four references with names, affiliations, e-mail addresses and mark those already asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification on cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the mathematical subject area(s) in which you have done research using the 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification printed on the back of this form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If listing more than one number, list first the one number which best describes your current primary interest. The back of the form lists the MSC codes (00–99) and topics for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement — award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For the cumulative influence of the total mathematical work of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include high level of research over a period of time, particular influence on the development of a field, and influence on mathematics through Ph.D. students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steele Prize for Mathematical Exposition — award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For a book or substantial survey or expository-research paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators should include a short description of the work that is the basis of the nomination, including complete bibliographic citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steele Prize for Seminal Contributions to Research — award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For a paper, whether recent or not, that has proved to be of fundamental or lasting importance in its field, or a model of important work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators should include a short description of the work that is the basis of the nomination, including complete bibliographic citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award for Distinguished Public Service — award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented every two years to a research mathematician who has made a distinguished contribution to the mathematics profession during the preceding five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nominations, include a short description of the pertinent activities of the nominee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frank Nelson Cole Prizes — award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Prizes awarded at five-year intervals for contributions to algebra and number theory, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations should include a short description of the work that is the basis of the nomination, including complete bibliographic citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize — award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded every two years to recognize an outstanding contribution to mathematics research by a woman in the previous five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators should include a short description of the work that is the basis of the nomination, including complete bibliographic citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS prize nomination submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements for submitting nominations for AMS prizes and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations with supporting information should be submitted to the Secretary (Robert M. Fossum, Department of Mathematics, University of Illinois, 1409 West Green Street, Urbana, IL 61801). For the Steele Prizes, include a short description of the work that is the basis of the nomination, including complete bibliographic citations. For the Public Service Award, include a short description of the pertinent activities. For the Cole and Satter Prizes, include a short description of the work and complete bibliographic citations. A curriculum vitae should be included for all nominees. Nominations will be forwarded to the appropriate prize selection committee. Deadline for nominations is March 31, 1996.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC National Science Education Standards — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Science Education Standards provide comprehensive guidance to improve science education in grades K–12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Standards offer specific guidelines for science content, science teaching, professional development of teachers, assessment, science education programs, and the science education system. Copies available from the National Academy Press (phone and web contact provided).
